featured.name: Feeroute
featured.tagline: Public fee vaults for Pons v2 creators on Robinhood Chain. A vault receives a token's creator fees and splits them by fixed shares (up to 10 wallets, optional vesting), and any change waits out a per-vault timelock. Anyone can sweep, and a bot sweeps hourly.
featured.audit: Not audited by a third party. The docs say "Beta, not audited" and describe an internal line-by-line review.
contracts: not a proxy (no proxy slots; Sourcify isProxy=false)
FeerouteVault (one per token, created by the factory)
source included in the factory's verified bundle
not verified itself; bytecode matches the verified PonsV2LauncherToken template
facts: Scanned Oct 20, 2026. FeerouteFactory: 19/100 LOW. The only flags are a fresh deployer (2 transactions, first seen Oct 17) and a domain registered Oct 18. $FEEROUTE: 36/100 MODERATE. Drivers: Pons v2 curve liquidity around $4k, a launch wallet first seen Oct 19, and the new domain. No mint, pause or blacklist functions.

The factory has no owner() and no admin functions. createVault can only be called by a token's current Pons creator-fee recipient, and it checks that the curve is ETH-quoted. It is bound to the Pons v2 launch factory 0x7eD5…EC7e, matching the docs.
Vaults use Ownable2Step and ReentrancyGuard. Only ETH is split, and recipients that fail are credited, not dropped. The creator cap and timelock are fixed at creation.
The timelock is chosen per vault, from 0 to 30 days, so it is not one fixed value. The site's example shows 48 hours, and Explore lets you filter for vaults with the timelock off.
At block 93,604,758 the factory had created 0 vaults (no VaultCreated events). The $FEEROUTE token's Pons creator-fee recipient is still its launch wallet, not a Feeroute vault.

The docs list these limits themselves: the creator cap covers only the owner's own address; ownership transfer and rescueToken (ERC-20s go to the owner) have no timelock; fee flow after graduation to Uniswap v4 is unverified; and the Pons admin can reroute fees through Pons' own 72-hour timelock.
questions: Will $FEEROUTE's own creator fees be routed through a Feeroute vault, and with what split and timelock? That would be the clearest demo for holders.
Could the $FEEROUTE token be verified on Blockscout or Sourcify? Today it only matches the Pons template bytecode.
The hourly sweep bot: which wallet runs it? Is its status shown on /status, and what happens to sweeps if it stops? Anyone can still call sweep().
Will the post-graduation (Uniswap v4) fee path be tested before the first routed token graduates?
Should rescueToken and ownership transfer go behind the same timelock as split changes in a later version, given the docs list both as known limits?

featured.name: Perma (Permapad)
featured.tagline: Bonding-curve token launchpad on Robinhood Chain; graduated liquidity goes to a locker with no withdraw path.
featured.audit: Permapad's Terms say the contracts have not had an outside audit.
contracts: EIP-1167 clone of a verified implementation
facts: All eight core contracts listed in the app are verified (Sourcify exact match). None is a proxy: the EIP-1967 implementation, admin and beacon slots are empty, so the code cannot be swapped.

PermaLocker has no function that removes liquidity. Its state-changing functions are a one-time deployer initialize (already done), graduate, zapLiquidity, buyBackAndBurn and releaseBurn. That matches the site's claim that locked liquidity cannot be withdrawn.

Governance is in its owner-key phase. PermaGovernor.ownerKey() is 0xAD71…6533, a plain wallet (no contract code). It can run the governor's whitelisted actions directly, but never the treasury sweeps switch.

Holder voting opens at handoverAt() = Dec 2, 2026, 10:42 AM PST (fee manager T0 + 45 days; T0 was Oct 18, 2026, 11:42 AM PDT). The owner key keeps its powers alongside voting until T0 + 365 days, unless it steps down or holders vote it out (possible from day 90).

The same wallet is the service-settings key (PermaServiceSettings.key()). That key can pause new launches on the factory, but the code comments say it can never change coins that are already launched.

Score note: our scanner flags a withdraw(uint256) selector in the factory bytecode. In the verified source this is the factory calling WETH.withdraw to unwrap refunds, not a privileged rescue function.
questions: Is the owner key / service key (0xAD71…6533) a hardware wallet? Is a move to a multisig planned? proposeOwnerKey/acceptOwnerKey already support a two-step handover.
Can you publish the governor's whitelist (target, function, tier) in plain language, so holders can see exactly what the owner key can change before Dec 2?
Is an outside review planned before holder governance opens?

featured.name: COWL
featured.tagline: Private receive links on Robinhood Chain: ERC-5564 stealth payments through a small router with no owner.
facts: Not a mixer. The router has no pool and holds no funds. sendEth/sendToken forward each payment straight from the sender to a one-time (stealth) address, then log one ERC-5564 announcement. Amounts and senders stay public, as the site says. So we scored it; mixer-style pools are excluded from Launch Watch.
No owner, admin, fee or upgrade path: the verified source has no state variables and no privileged functions, and the EIP-1967 slots are empty.
sendToken only pulls tokens from msg.sender. An approval to the router cannot be spent by anyone else.
The router was deployed Oct 18, 2026, 1:44 PM PDT, from a new wallet. The domain was registered the same day, and those two facts make up most of the automated score.
$COWL has not launched yet (Pons, Oct 19, 2026, 6:00 AM PDT). There is no token contract to score yet.
questions: The announcement records the requested amount. For fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens, the stealth address receives less than announced. Does the Inbox show live balances rather than announced amounts?
Anyone can post an ERC-5564 announcement directly to the public announcer. Does the Inbox check that an announced payment actually arrived before showing it?
Will the $COWL token contract be verified at launch, and will its owner/fee settings be published next to the router on cowl.pro?
